Session: Theory briefing: models propose and engineering systems verify, repository instructions, mechanisms (rules, skills, hooks), task contracts, local multi-repo workspace with GitHub MCP, model routing, evidence (theory-presentation.html).
Outcome: Shared vocabulary and the map for the demos.

Session: Demo 00 — Prompt Audit: audit a CLAUDE.md and prune filler while keeping MSVC flags.
Demo 01 — Caveman: concise status reports without evidence loss.
Outcome: Shorter reports that keep errors, targets, and unverified platforms.

Session: Demo 02 — Noisy CI (RTK): filtered build and test output.
Outcome: Compact logs that keep the failing test, line, and summary.

Session: Demo 03 — Ponytail: smallest correct fix for a 32-bit/64-bit range-check bug.
Outcome: A minimal fix with test evidence per target.

Session: Demo 04 — Contract vs Prompt: the same task with a vague prompt and with a contract (C++ or Go).
Demo 05 — Rules & Guardrails: plan tests first and keep domain logic pure.
Demo 06 — Hooks: block destructive commands; flag x86/x64 and syntax problems after every edit.
Outcome: One hook the team could adopt.

Session: Demo 07 — Ticket to PR: ticket, spec on Opus, implementation on Sonnet in a fresh context, verification, adversarial review (see MODEL-ROUTING.md).
Outcome: A reusable loop and a model-routing rule to test.

Session: Wrap-up: pick 3–5 rules for the team's CLAUDE.md, choose one real task for the loop, share READING-LIST.md.
